meta.description: Designs and analyzes in vivo CRISPR screens in animal tumor models, organoids, and immune-cell adoptive transfers. Covers bottleneck math (250x cells/sgRNA requires ~25M cells implanted; impossible for most syngeneic models, forcing focused libraries), focused library design (Manguso 2017 Nature 547:413 immune screen; Chen 2015 tumor screens), CRISPR-StAR intrinsic-control screening (Uijttewaal 2025 Nat Biotechnol 43:1848), clonal-dynamics-limited detection, tumor-explant DNA recovery, syngeneic vs xenograft vs PDX considerations, and the relationship to downstream MAGeCK / drugZ analysis.

scientific_integrity.detail: All citations (Manguso 2017 Nature 547:413, Chen 2015 Cell 160:1246, Lee 2023 Cancer Gene Ther 30:1610, Scheidmann 2022 Cancer Res 82:681, Uijttewaal 2025 Nat Biotechnol 43:1848) are specific, real, and accurately summarized. No output across the 5 tested inputs fabricated a p-value, sample size, or effect size; Input 4's real MAGeCK/meta-analysis numbers were all produced by actual code execution on disclosed-synthetic data.

practice_boundaries.detail: This is animal-model research-protocol design, not human diagnosis or treatment; no patient-facing medical claims were made in any output, so no clinical disclaimer is required.

methodological_ground.detail: No statistical fallacy (e.g. correlation-as-causation, mismatched test) found in the Skill or in any of the 5 outputs. Flagged separately (see P1 recommendation, not a veto trigger): SKILL.md and usage-guide.md never mention IACUC / institutional animal-ethics approval anywhere, despite the Skill covering live-animal tumor implantation and sacrifice throughout -- confirmed by a full-text grep for 'IACUC|ethic|welfare|approval|humane|3Rs|institutional' returning zero hits. This is a documentation omission worth fixing, not a methodological fallacy that invalidates any output's conclusions, so it is scored PASS with a P1 recommendation rather than failing the gate.

code_usability.detail: All executed code ran without syntax errors or missing dependencies: mageck test (6/6 animals), mageck mle (design-matrix run), and the bundled examples/per_animal_meta_analysis.py's exact groupby().apply() call (verified separately with DeprecationWarning/FutureWarning promoted to errors -- no warning raised on pandas 3.0.5).

functional_suitability.note: Covers the full design-to-hit-calling arc (bottleneck math, focused library, CRISPR-StAR, model choice, DNA recovery, hit calling, diagnostics) with correct, checkable arithmetic. Minor gap: no concrete cell-number/MOI worked example for genome-scale CRISPR-StAR (found in Input 2).

reliability.note: Version-compatibility section instructs introspection when APIs differ; quantitative thresholds table and failure-mode table function as built-in sanity checks. Bundled script hard-stops with FileNotFoundError when no per-animal files are found -- correct defensive design for Category 3 per the Scene Override, not a defect.

performance_context.note: SKILL.md is ~240 lines, usage-guide.md ~135 -- reasonably token-efficient for the scope covered; a few tables (Quantitative Thresholds, Common Errors) slightly duplicate content already in the body prose.

agent_usability.note: Clear trigger phrases, a numbered 12-step 'What the Agent Will Do' workflow in usage-guide.md, and consistent terminology across both files (verified: 'CEGv2 PR-AUC >0.4', '10+ animals', 'focused library 3,000-15,000 sgRNAs' repeated identically in SKILL.md, usage-guide.md, and Common Errors table).

human_usability.note: Quick Start, Example Prompts, Decision Cheat Sheet, and Validation Checklist give strong discoverability; forgiveness is good (Common Errors table maps symptom -> cause -> fix).

security.note: No credential handling, no eval/exec of raw strings, no prompt-injection surface; all bundled code (per_animal_meta_analysis.py) only reads local TSVs and calls scipy/pandas/statsmodels.

maintainability.note: Shipped-means-present check passed: the one file SKILL.md points to (examples/per_animal_meta_analysis.py) exists and runs as documented. Only one bundled script for a Skill this broad, and no automated tests bundled.

agent_specific.note: Strong trigger precision (139-word description covering many specific scenarios) and composability (8-entry Related Skills list, all real crispr-screens/pathway-analysis skill paths). Docked 3 points: the compound hit-calling threshold in the bundled example is fragile under realistic per-animal power (Input 4 finding), and the MLE path's permutation-based FDR values are non-deterministic run-to-run with no seed-control flag exposed by MAGeCK 0.5.9.5, undocumented by the Skill.

inputs.label: Per-animal MAGeCK + Stouffer meta-analysis on 6-animal synthetic in vivo screen (executed)
inputs.note: Fully executed (Mode D). mageck test run on 6 synthetic animals vs plasmid (RRA); bundled Stouffer meta-analysis script run unmodified on the real gene_summary.txt outputs. Meta-analysis correctly ranked all 5 planted true hits at the top (meta-z 3.7-5.3, meta-FDR down to 3e-6), but the documented compound threshold (meta-FDR<0.05 AND >=50% of animals individually at per-animal FDR<0.05) yielded 0 called hits because per-animal RRA power was too low for any single animal to cross FDR<0.05 -- a real, reproducible finding, disclosed rather than hidden. mageck test itself re-ran byte-identical (T3 determinism confirmed); a separate mageck mle run on the same data showed permutation-derived FDR columns drifting between runs (Wald p-values and betas stayed identical) -- documented as a P2/P1 finding, not used to fail this input since the Skill's primary path (RRA+meta) avoids it.

key_strengths: Bottleneck math and coverage thresholds are internally consistent and match the worked usage-guide.md examples exactly (verified: 2M cells / 8,000 sgRNAs = 250x).

The bundled per-animal Stouffer meta-analysis script (examples/per_animal_meta_analysis.py) ran unmodified on real MAGeCK output and correctly ranked all 5 planted true hits above 55 background noise genes (meta-FDR as low as 3e-6).

The Skill's primary recommended hit-calling path (MAGeCK RRA via mageck test) is fully deterministic -- verified by re-running on identical synthetic data and diffing gene_summary.txt byte-for-byte with zero differences.
Extensive, real, verifiable citations (Manguso 2017 Nature 547:413, Uijttewaal 2025 Nat Biotechnol 43:1848, Chen 2015 Cell 160:1246, Lee 2023, Scheidmann 2022) with correctly stated findings.

Failure-mode and Common Errors tables predict real behavior observed in testing: the 'per-animal hit lists differ / clonal dominance' entry accurately anticipates the compound hit-calling threshold's zero-hit outcome found in Input 4.

recommendations.title: No mention anywhere of IACUC / institutional animal-ethics approval
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md and usage-guide.md describe live-animal tumor implantation, tamoxifen induction, and tumor harvest/sacrifice across every design pattern, but never mention institutional animal-care-and-use committee (IACUC) approval or any ethical-review requirement.
recommendations.root_cause: The Skill was written purely as a quantitative/statistical design guide and never added a standing ethics-compliance note.
recommendations.fix: Add a one-line standing requirement to the Prerequisites section of both SKILL.md and usage-guide.md: 'All procedures require prior IACUC (or equivalent institutional) approval; this Skill assumes approval is already in place and does not itself provide ethical review.'

recommendations.title: Compound hit-calling threshold can report zero hits despite strong meta-signal
recommendations.problem: The bundled per-animal meta-analysis's hit-calling rule (meta-FDR<0.05 AND >=50% of animals individually at per-animal FDR<0.05) called 0/5 planted true hits even though the 5 planted genes were unambiguously the top 5 by meta-z and meta-FDR (down to 3e-6), because per-animal MAGeCK RRA power was too low for any single animal to individually cross FDR<0.05.
recommendations.root_cause: The per-animal consistency requirement assumes each animal's own RRA test has enough power to reach FDR<0.05 on its own, which does not hold for typical in vivo cohort sizes and gene-universe sizes -- exactly the scenario this Skill exists to handle.
recommendations.fix: Document the minimum per-animal power needed for the strict consistency rule to ever fire, and offer a documented fallback (e.g., meta-FDR-only threshold, or a per-animal nominal-p rather than FDR consistency check) for realistic cohort sizes.

recommendations.title: MAGeCK MLE's permutation-based FDR values are non-deterministic run-to-run, undocumented
recommendations.problem: Re-running 'mageck mle' (the Skill's Option A) on identical count data and design matrix produced different permutation-derived FDR-like p-values between runs (effect sizes and Wald p-values stayed identical); MAGeCK 0.5.9.5 exposes no --seed flag to control this.
recommendations.root_cause: MLE's default variance/permutation modeling draws from an unseeded random process with no user-facing seed control in the underlying tool.
recommendations.fix: Add a note to the MLE section of SKILL.md that permutation-derived FDR columns are not exactly reproducible run-to-run, and recommend reporting Wald p-values (which are stable) as the primary significance metric, or increasing --permutation-round for more stable estimates.

recommendations.title: CRISPR-StAR section lacks a concrete genome-scale worked example
recommendations.problem: Unlike the focused-library section, the CRISPR-StAR section gives no worked cell-number/MOI example, so an agent following the Skill for a genome-scale screen cannot verify feasibility the way it can for a focused library.
recommendations.root_cause: The section was written narratively from Uijttewaal 2025's qualitative description without porting over any of the paper's own quantitative design parameters.
recommendations.fix: Add a worked numeric example analogous to the Manguso 2017 bottleneck-math example, using Uijttewaal 2025's actual reported cell numbers and MOI.
